databaseName: Section 2 - Data Ingestion and Storage Vocabulary

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a family of standards for operating system compatibility. EFS is a POSIX file system, meaning it uses standard APIs like ls, rm, etc. It provides Unix-like file system semantics.
answers.actualAnswerText: POSIX (Portable Operating System Interface)

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ uses Customer Provided Key. Client manages key, key is sent in header with every request, AWS does not store this key, HTTPS only. Client must provide same key for get/fetch operations.
answers.actualAnswerText: SSE-C (Server-Side Encryption with Customer-provided keys)

answers.questionText: What is "KMS (Key Management Service)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: KMS is AWS Key Management Service. SSE-KMS uses AWS Key Manager. EFS uses KMS for encryption at rest. Kinesis and MSK use KMS for at-rest encryption.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is AWS Simple Queue Service. S3 events can be sent to SNS, SQS, Lambda, or EventBridge. You must create resource policies to allow S3 to write to these services.
answers.actualAnswerText: SQS (Simple Queue Service)

answers.questionText: What is "ETL (Extract, Transform, Load)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: ETL is a data integration process that involves three steps: Extract (fetch data from sources like API, disk, etc.), Transform (convert from source to target format, clean, enrich, aggregate, calculations, encoding/decoding, handle missing data), and Load (move to target destination). Velocity affects load strategy (batch, realtime, streaming). Used with Data Warehouses which use Schema-on-Write.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ holds vast amounts of raw data with no preprocessing. It supports batch, real-time, and streaming data. Uses Schema-on-Read (ELT) where structure is applied after the fact using services like Athena and Glue. Can store structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data. Examples include S3, Azure data lake store, and Hadoop. Generally less expensive and more agile than Data Warehouses.
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Lake

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Java Management Extensions, a Java technology for managing and monitoring applications. MSK Prometheus monitoring uses JMX export metrics on node exporter.
answers.actualAnswerText: JMX (Java Management Extensions)

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is AWS data warehouse service. It is an example of a Data Warehouse system, designed for complete queries using structured schemas.
answers.actualAnswerText: Redshift

answers.questionText: What is "S3 Prefix"?
answers.actualAnswerText: S3 Prefix is the path portion of an S3 object key. For example, in s3://bucket-name/the/path/to/item.ext, the prefix is "/the/path/to/". S3 performance is measured by prefix, not bucket. There are no actual directories in S3, but the UI creates the appearance of folders.
answers.userAnswerText: Url segment, not file name or bucket name

answers.questionText: What is "EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: EC2 is AWS Elastic Compute Cloud. EBS volumes attach to EC2 instances. EFS can be mounted to multiple EC2 instances. FSx for Windows can move with EC2.

answers.questionText: What is "MSK Serverless"?
answers.actualAnswerText: MSK Serverless is hands-free configuration where you define topics and number of partitions per topic. Security is IAM access control. Pricing: $0.75 per cluster hour, $0.0015 partition hour, $0.10 GB storage per month, $0.10 ingress GB, $0.05 egress GB.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a columnar storage format similar to Parquet, optimized for reading and writing data. Used with systems like Hive and Hadoop for efficient analytics workloads.
answers.actualAnswerText: ORC (Optimized Row Columnar)

answers.questionText: What is "SSE-KMS (Server-Side Encryption with AWS KMS managed keys)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: SSE-KMS uses AWS Key Management Service. Client code specifies which key to use. Usage can be logged in CloudTrail (good for audit/compliance). Requires header: x-amz-server-side-encryption: "aws:kms". May require further API calls which can introduce latency.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ sits between Bucket and Access Point and acts as a transformation layer. You can have several Access Points calling different Lambda functions to transform data differently. Origin data remains unchanged but provides different "views" of the data.
answers.actualAnswerText: S3 Object Lambda

answers.questionText: What is "EFS-Archive"?
answers.actualAnswerText: EFS-Archive is an EFS storage class for rarely accessed files (few times a year), 50% cheaper than standard. Implement lifecycle policy to move files between tiers.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Elastic Block Store, a network-attached storage volume for EC2 instances. Data persists after instances are terminated. Can be configured to delete on termination. Root drive (drv0) auto-deletes by default, but this can be overwritten. Bound to one AZ, can make snapshot and transport to other AZ.
answers.actualAnswerText: EBS (Elastic Block Store)
answers.answerNotes: The answer is in the question

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a unit of capacity in Kinesis Data Stream. Each shard inbound 1MB/s or 1000 records/second, each shard outbound 2MB/s. Provisioned Mode uses shards for capacity. Hot shard occurs when one shard receives more data than others.
answers.actualAnswerText: Kinesis Shard

answers.questionText: What is "S3 Bucket"?
answers.actualAnswerText: S3 Bucket is the main container in S3. Buckets must be globally unique across all AWS accounts and regions. Buckets are defined regionally but appear as a global service. There are two types: "general purpose" and "directory" (directory type is out of scope for exam).

answers.questionText: What is "Lambda"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Lambda is AWS serverless compute service. S3 events can be sent to Lambda. Kinesis Firehose can transform using Lambda at receiver. S3 Object Lambda sits between Bucket and Access Point for data transformation.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is one of the three V's of data properties. It refers to the types of data: Structured/Unstructured. Sources include API, Stream, Human input, and electronic devices (mobile devices).
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Variety

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a data integration process that involves three steps: Extract (fetch data from sources like API, disk, etc.), Transform (convert from source to target format, clean, enrich, aggregate, calculations, encoding/decoding, handle missing data), and Load (move to target destination). Velocity affects load strategy (batch, realtime, streaming). Used with Data Warehouses which use Schema-on-Write.
answers.actualAnswerText: ETL (Extract, Transform, Load)

answers.questionText: What is "SSL (Secure Sockets Layer)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: SSL is Secure Sockets Layer, a predecessor to TLS. S3 uses SSL/TLS and HTTPS for in-flight encryption. AWS recommends bucket policy requiring aws:SecureTransport.

answers.questionText: What is "OpenZFS"?
answers.actualAnswerText: OpenZFS is an open-source file system. FSx for OpenZFS provides managed OpenZFS on AWS with high performance characteristics.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a centralized service for maintaining configuration information and providing distributed synchronization. MSK creates and manages Kafka Broker and ZooKeeper nodes.
answers.actualAnswerText: ZooKeeper

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Kinesis Client Library, an SDK library optimized for standard Kinesis consumer operations. Best practice for reading data from Kinesis.
answers.actualAnswerText: KCL (Kinesis Client Library)

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a legacy system designed for complete queries using "Star" or "Snowflake" structured schemas. It uses Schema-on-Write (ETL), is optimized to read headers, and is designed for structured data. Examples include Redshift, Google Big Data Query, and Azure SQL Data warehouse. Generally more expensive and less agile than Data Lakes.
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Warehouse

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is AWS Elastic Compute Cloud. EBS volumes attach to EC2 instances. EFS can be mounted to multiple EC2 instances. FSx for Windows can move with EC2.
answers.actualAnswerText: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)

answers.questionText: What is "S3 (Simple Storage Service)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Amazon S3 is an object storage service used for backup, recovery, storage, static websites, archives, hybrid storage, app hosting, media hosting, and big data analytics. Uses buckets (main containers) and items/objects (files). Buckets must be globally unique and are defined regionally.

answers.questionText: What is "Data Variety"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Variety is one of the three V's of data properties. It refers to the types of data: Structured/Unstructured. Sources include API, Stream, Human input, and electronic devices (mobile devices).

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a fully managed Windows Share. Supports NTFS and SMB, can move with EC2 (different EC2 can connect), ACLs, user quotas, supports Microsoft's Distributed File System (DFS). Scales up to 10's GB/s, millions of IOPS, 1000's of petabytes. Storage options: SSD/HDD. Supports multiple AZ. Uses S3 for backups. Can connect via DirectConnect or VPN.
answers.actualAnswerText: FSx for Windows

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is AWS fully managed ETL service. Data Lakes use Schema-on-Read where structure is applied after the fact using services like Athena and Glue. Glue is considered reliable for pipeline management. Data Mesh uses self-service tooling and infrastructure like Glue.
answers.actualAnswerText: Glue

answers.questionText: What is "Flink"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Flink is Apache Flink, an open-source stream processing framework. MSAF is AWS's managed version. Flink is used for real-time stream processing and analytics.

answers.questionText: What is "EFS-Standard"?
answers.actualAnswerText: EFS-Standard is the EFS storage class for frequent use. It supports multi-AZ and is the default tier for EFS.
answers.answerNotes: Respone and question needs more specific

answers.questionText: What is "HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: HTTPS is HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure. SSE-C requires HTTPS only. S3 uses HTTPS for secure data transfer.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Server Message Block protocol, used for file sharing in Windows networks. FSx for Windows supports SMB protocol.
answers.actualAnswerText: SMB (Server Message Block)

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is S3 Cross Region Replication, used for compliance, lower latency, cross-account replication. Replication is async, requires versioning, can be cross-account, and only works for new items.
answers.actualAnswerText: CRR (Cross Region Replication)

answers.questionText: What is "Kafka Partition"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Kafka Partition is a division of a topic. MSK Serverless allows you to define number of partitions per topic. Data is organized by topic/partition in MSK.

answers.questionText: What is "VPN (Virtual Private Network)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: VPN is Virtual Private Network. FSx for Windows and FSx for Lustre can connect via DirectConnect or VPN.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is one of the three V's of data properties. It refers to how fast data is generated and processed: Batch Process, Real-time, or Near Real-time. Examples include IoT data, sensor data, and high frequency trades.
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Velocity

answers.questionText: What is "Kinesis Consumer"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Kinesis Consumer reads data from Kinesis Streams. Consumers can be applications, Lambda, Firehose, etc. KCL (Kinesis Client Library) is optimized for standard operations.

answers.questionText: What is "ACL (Access Control List)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: ACL is Access Control List. In S3, Object ACL and Bucket ACL can be disabled. ACLs provide fine-grained access control at the object or bucket level.
answers.answerNotes: Answer should better mention bucket and object

answers.questionText: What is "Impala"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Impala is a SQL query engine for Hadoop. Parquet format is used with Impala for analytics workloads.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is AWS Identity and Access Management. In S3, IAM principal can access IFF: (IAM permission allow) OR (Resource permission allow) AND there are no deny. Principle can be user or service (not owner).
answers.actualAnswerText: IAM (Identity and Access Management)

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is a type of Life Cycle Rule action that moves objects from tier to tier (e.g., after 60 days, after 6 months to Glacier).
answers.actualAnswerText: S3 Transition Action

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is hands-free configuration where you define topics and number of partitions per topic. Security is IAM access control. Pricing: $0.75 per cluster hour, $0.0015 partition hour, $0.10 GB storage per month, $0.10 ingress GB, $0.05 egress GB.
answers.actualAnswerText: MSK Serverless

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Transport Layer Security, a cryptographic protocol for secure communication. MSK uses in-flight TLS, at rest EBS encryption. S3 uses SSL/TLS and HTTPS for in-flight encryption.
answers.actualAnswerText: TLS (Transport Layer Security)

answers.questionText: What is "JDBC (Java Database Connectivity)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: JDBC is a Java-based API for database connectivity. It is platform independent but language dependent (Java).

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Network File System protocol. EFS uses NFSv4.1 Protocol. It allows multiple clients to access shared files over a network.
answers.actualAnswerText: NFS (Network File System)

answers.questionText: What is "Glue"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Glue is AWS fully managed ETL service. Data Lakes use Schema-on-Read where structure is applied after the fact using services like Athena and Glue. Glue is considered reliable for pipeline management. Data Mesh uses self-service tooling and infrastructure like Glue.
answers.userAnswerText: Sql like but can use multiple source, s3, Redshift aethena

answers.questionText: What is "Data Volume"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Volume is one of the three V's of data properties. It refers to the size or amount of data: GB, TB, PB. It concerns how we store it, how we access it, and what preprocessing concerns exist.

answers.questionText: What is "EFS (Elastic File System)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: EFS is Elastic File System, a managed network file system that can be mounted to multiple EC2 instances simultaneously across multiple AZs. It scales automatically, supports NFSv4.1 Protocol, is not Windows compatible (requires Linux AMI), uses Security Groups to control access, KMS for encryption at rest, POSIX file system. Costs approximately 3x GP2, pay per use/access (not allocated).

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is AWS Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow. It is one of the ETL/ELT Pipeline Orchestration Services in AWS, along with Event Bridge, Step Functions, and Glue Workflow.
answers.actualAnswerText: MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is an identifier for object versions when versioning is enabled. When versionId is null, it indicates the bucket has versioning enabled but the item was likely created before versioning was enabled.
answers.actualAnswerText: S3 versionId

answers.questionText: What is "Data Warehouse"?
answers.actualAnswerText: A data warehouse is a legacy system designed for complete queries using "Star" or "Snowflake" structured schemas. It uses Schema-on-Write (ETL), is optimized to read headers, and is designed for structured data. Examples include Redshift, Google Big Data Query, and Azure SQL Data warehouse. Generally more expensive and less agile than Data Lakes.

answers.questionText: Fill in the blank: __________ is Input/Output Operations Per Second, a performance metric for storage systems. EBS volumes are allocated in Size and/or IOPS. Elastic Volume can change IOPS on the fly.
answers.actualAnswerText: IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second)

answers.questionText: What is "Data Velocity"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Data Velocity is one of the three V's of data properties. It refers to how fast data is generated and processed: Batch Process, Real-time, or Near Real-time. Examples include IoT data, sensor data, and high frequency trades.

answers.questionText: What is "IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: IOPS is Input/Output Operations Per Second, a performance metric for storage systems. EBS volumes are allocated in Size and/or IOPS. Elastic Volume can change IOPS on the fly.

answers.questionText: What is "Athena"?
answers.actualAnswerText: Athena is AWS interactive query service. Data Lakes use Schema-on-Read where structure is applied after the fact using services like Athena and Glue.
answers.userAnswerText: Schema on read,  support s3, Redshift others

answers.actualAnswerText: Athena

answers.questionText: What is "SNS (Simple Notification Service)"?
answers.actualAnswerText: SNS is AWS Simple Notification Service. S3 events can be sent to SNS, SQS, Lambda, or EventBridge. You must create resource policies to allow S3 to write to these services.
